**STEP 3 - Items:** Red grapes (about 22) and green grapes (2). No oil or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The grapes cover a loose cluster of about 25% of the plate, roughly 100 cm². Red grapes take about 22% and green grapes about 3%.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole fruit has a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml, so 180 ml × 0.6 ≈ 110 g. Splitting this across the two colours gives about 110 g of red grapes and 10 g of green grapes. A per-grape check (about 5 g each for 24 grapes, roughly 120 g) agrees.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Grapes are about 69 kcal/100 g. Red grapes: 110 g × 0.69 ≈ 76 kcal. Green grapes: 10 g × 0.67 ≈ 7 kcal. Total ≈ 83 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 120 g of grapes, roughly 24 small grapes, fits a small handful on a 20 cm plate. The estimate is plausible.
